content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Courses teachable

Each platform you use to sell digital products offers a unique set of features, but they're not designed to give you ownership or control. With Teachable, you're locked into their ecosystem, relying on their payment processing and limited features. Gumroad allows more flexibility, but still takes a significant cut of your sales. PayPal, as mentioned, is notorious for its account suspensions, leaving you with no access to your funds. Stripe, although widely used, is only available in 46 countries. Each of these options comes with its own set of trade-offs, but they're all built on the same flawed assumption: that the platform will always be there to serve you.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

The real issue with these platforms is how they handle restricted countries. Teachable, for example, requires a bank account or Stripe Connect to process payments, making it inaccessible to creators in many countries. Gumroad allows some flexibility, but still has strict rules around account verification and payment processing. PayPal's account suspensions are a major concern, especially in countries with a history of financial isolation. And Stripe, as mentioned, is only available in 46 countries. This is where a sovereign commerce infrastructure comes in – it's not bound by the same rules and regulations, allowing creators to sell their digital products without restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, each platform has its own set of rules. Teachable charges a 0% payment processing fee, but takes a 10% transaction fee. Gumroad charges 3.5% + $0.30 per sale, plus a payment processing fee. PayPal charges 2.9% + $0.30 per sale, plus a payment processing fee. Stripe charges 2.9% + $0.30 per sale, plus a payment processing fee. A sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, charges a flat 0.5% fee for all transactions, with no additional payment processing fees. This means more of your money stays with you, not the platform.
A sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround, but a permanent structural alternative to the platforms that have held you back.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

One of the biggest advantages of a sovereign commerce infrastructure is ownership, automation, and delivery. With each platform, you're locked into their ecosystem, relying on their payment processing and limited features. But with a sovereign commerce infrastructure, you own everything after deployment – no platform dependencies, no subscriptions, and lifetime access. This means you can automate your sales, delivery, and customer support, freeing up time for what matters most: creating and selling your digital products.
